routes.title: Samarkand in one day
routes.eyebrow: From Tashkent · private car with driver
routes.summary: An early start, the six landmarks of the city and back in the evening. They sit almost on one line, so you walk between most of them with only two short drives.

stops.name: Gur-e-Amir
stops.text: Timur's mausoleum. A ribbed turquoise dome outside, a gilded chamber inside; his sons and his grandson Ulugh Beg lie here too.

stops.name: Registan
stops.text: A square framed by three madrasahs: Ulugh Beg's (15th century), Sher-Dor with the lions on its portal, and Tilya-Kori with its gold hall. The picture everyone comes for.

stops.name: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
stops.text: The congregational mosque built under Timur. An enormous portal, and a stone Quran stand in the middle of the courtyard.

stops.name: Siyob Bazaar
stops.text: A working market right behind the mosque. Samarkand bread, dried fruit, nuts and spices — the easiest place to buy something to take home.

stops.name: Shah-i-Zinda
stops.text: A street of mausoleums climbing the hillside. The finest tilework in Samarkand, 14th–15th century.

stops.name: Ulugh Beg Observatory
stops.text: What remains of a giant sextant cut into the hill, and a museum about the 15th-century Samarkand school of astronomy.

included: Car with driver: Tashkent — Samarkand — Tashkent
Drives between the sites inside the city
tips: We leave at 06:00–07:00; any later and the sightseeing gets squeezed.
Instead of the car you can take the Afrosiyob high-speed train, about 2 hours each way. We can buy the tickets.
Midday is hot in summer: Shah-i-Zinda and the Registan are better in the morning or late afternoon.
Mosques ask for covered shoulders and knees; scarves for women are available at the entrance.
routes.priceNote: A full day with waiting and the return is priced separately. The one-way transfer starts at $200.

routes.title: Tashkent in one day
routes.summary: The city is spread out and does not walk well. A car and driver move you between the stops all day. This is the full list; a day usually fits five or six — we choose together.

stops.name: Hazrati Imam
stops.text: The religious heart of the city: the Barak Khan Madrasah, the Tilla Sheikh Mosque, and the Muyi Muborak library where the Uthman Quran is kept — one of the oldest copies in existence.

stops.name: Chorsu Bazaar
stops.text: The market under the blue dome. Rows of spices, dried fruit, meat and bread; the upper gallery is the place to see the dome from inside.

stops.name: Kukeldash Madrasah
stops.text: 16th century, on the rise above the bazaar. The courtyard is quiet the moment you step in from the noise.

stops.name: Amir Timur Square
stops.text: The park at the centre, with the Timur monument, the chiming clock and buildings from several eras around it.

stops.name: Metro: Kosmonavtlar and Alisher Navoi
stops.text: Two stations worth riding for the interiors: cosmonaut portraits on blue glass, and domed vaults. Photography is allowed.

stops.name: Minor Mosque
stops.text: A modern mosque of white marble with a turquoise dome, on the bank of the Ankhor canal.

stops.name: TV Tower
stops.text: 375 metres, with an observation deck. From here you see how green and how flat the city is.

included: Every drive between the stops of the day
tips: Some museums close on Mondays; we adjust the route.
Bring your passport for the TV Tower — it is checked at the entrance.
Photography is allowed in the metro, but not of military sites.
If you want a guide for the whole day, say so in advance: that is a separate service.

routes.title: Old Tashkent on foot
routes.eyebrow: Private excursion with a guide · 3–4 hours
routes.summary: A compact walk through the old part of the city: the religious complex, the residential mahallas and the bazaar. Everything is close; you walk from one to the next.

stops.name: Hazrati Imam
stops.text: The main square of the complex, the Tilla Sheikh Mosque and the Kaffal Shashi mausoleum. Your guide explains how the religious centre of the city came together.

stops.name: Muyi Muborak
stops.text: The library where the Uthman Quran lies under glass — one of the oldest surviving copies. Photography inside is restricted.

stops.name: Barak Khan Madrasah
stops.text: 16th century, with craft workshops around the courtyard: ceramics, metalwork, textiles.

stops.name: The mahalla around the complex
stops.text: Residential lanes: single-storey houses, gates, quiet courtyards. This is Tashkent off the parade route.

stops.name: Chorsu Bazaar
stops.text: The market under the blue dome. You taste bread, dried fruit and spices while the guide explains what things are called and what they should cost.

stops.name: Kukeldash Madrasah
stops.text: The last stop, on the rise above the bazaar: a quiet courtyard and a view back over the Chorsu dome.

included: A private guide for the whole walk
extra: Transport to the start and back
Food and shopping at the bazaar
tips: Wear walking shoes: part of the route is uneven paving.
Mosques ask for covered shoulders and knees.
In summer we walk before 11:00 or after 16:00.
More interested in food than architecture? Say so and the guide rebuilds the walk around the bazaar and the teahouses.

routes.title: A day in the mountains
routes.eyebrow: From Tashkent · private car with driver
routes.summary: One direction per day: Chimgan, Amirsoy, or Charvak with a walk in the canyon. All of them together does not fit into a day — we decide when confirming.

stops.name: Charvak Reservoir
stops.text: A viewpoint over turquoise water ringed by mountains. The beaches work in summer; in spring and autumn it is the view and the air.

stops.name: Chimgan and Beldersay
stops.text: A chairlift up, and the view of Great Chimgan — 3,309 metres. In winter this is the ski slope.

stops.name: Amirsoy
stops.text: A modern resort with a gondola, viewing decks and a restaurant at the top. The easiest option with children.

stops.name: Gulkam Canyon
stops.text: A short walk along the river between rock walls. The path is seasonal and depends on the water level — we check before we set off.

included: Private car with driver for the whole day
The agreed route out and back
tips: It is 5–10 degrees colder up there than in the city: bring a jacket even in summer.
Closed-toe shoes — the lifts and the paths require them.
Snow can close the road in winter; we confirm the route on the morning of the trip.
Gulkam is not always passable after rain — we will offer an alternative.
